Photo by Werner Slocum, NLR National Laboratory of the Rockies | 27 Renewable Diesel Renewable Diesel • Renewable diesel is produced from fats and oils, such as waste greases and animal fats and soybean oil, and is processed to be chemically equivalent to petroleum diesel. • Renewable diesel can be used as a replacement for petroleum diesel or blended with petroleum diesel. • Renewable diesel offers many benefits, including: ◦ Engine and infrastructure compatibility—Renewable diesel meets the ASTM D975 specification, which allows it to be used in diesel engines and existing infrastructure. ◦ Greater flexibility—Renewable diesel is a replacement for diesel. It can be blended with any amount of diesel or can fully replace diesel. Renewable diesel can be made from multiple feedstocks, and can be made at plants that also produce aviation fuel. Source: Alternative Fuels Data Center, Renewable Diesel, n.d. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 28 Biodiesel Fuel Biodiesel Fuel • Biodiesel is a biodegradable fuel made from animal fats, vegetable oils, or recycled cooking oil (ASTM D6751) (NREL, 2024) • Biodiesel is manufactured domestically and is a substitute for petroleum diesel. • Biodiesel and conventional diesel vehicles are the same. Although light-, medium-, and heavy-duty diesel vehicles are not alternative fuel vehicles, almost all can run on biodiesel blends. ◦ Before using biodiesel, check your engine original equipment manufacturer (OEM) recommendations to determine the allowable blend for your vehicle • Biodiesel fueling stations are available across the United States. ◦ Some state laws require petroleum diesel to contain a small percentage of biodiesel. • Using biodiesel as a vehicle fuel improves public health and the environment, provides safety benefits, and contributes to a resilient transportation system. ◦ In its pure, unblended form biodiesel causes less damage than petroleum diesel if spilled or released to the environment. ◦ It is less combustible than petroleum diesel. ◦ Biodiesel can improve lubricity of diesel fuel, reduces friction within the moving parts and avoiding additional wear. Source: Alternative Fuels Data Center, Biodiesel Fuel Basics, n.d. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 29 Considerations Considerations • What are your transportation requirements?
